full_judgment: 11. The appellate court, on examination of the plaintiffs' kabala-the exhibit-2 detected That the stamp panels of that kabala were purchased in the names of Ridhya Sundari of village-Ahmedpur and Badiul Alam of village-Charkalidas, Police Station-Sonagazi on two different dates long before the alleged date of execution of the said kabala. The appellate cowl took into consideration the fact that though according to the plaintiffs case Sirajul Islam paid the full consideration money to Biadhan Bia in the year 1950 when talk for sale allegedly took place, but the kabala was executed in the last part of 1951 and it was registered 3 months 21 days after the execution. Finding no explanation as to this delay in execution and registration of this kabala-the exhibit-2 and as to the fact that the stamp papers or this kith were purchased in the name of some 3rd party long before on two different dates from the side of the plaintiff the appellate court disbelieved the genuineness of this plaintiffs kabala the Exhibit-2. The appellate court also took into consideration that the P.W.3-the attesting witness of the exhibit-2 stated in his deposition that he did not see the execution of the said deed. Controverting the trial court's observation and findings the appellate court observed that there was actually no anomaly in the defendants' deed-the exhibit-Uma/4. The appellate court pointed out that this exhibit Uma/4 was registered within 15 days of its execution and the stamp paper of this deed also were purchased in the name of purchaser Bader Rahman. The appellate court in his judgment has also specifically mentioned that though the defendants could not file the original copy of exhibit-Uma/4 in the trial court they filed the same before the appellate court which the appellate court marked as exhibit-Uma(6) being 30 years old document. Rejecting the trial court's observation the appellate court found out that the date of execution of this deed is 25.11.1951 and not 25.11.1952.
